- Rates: 21% / 9% / 0% (Wet OB 1968 art. 9, Tabel I and II). 2026 change: Tabel I post b11 (logies) is repealed, so short-stay accommodation is 21% from 1 Jan 2026, including 2025 prepayments for 2026 stays. Culture, sport and camping (posts b3, b10, b14) stay at 9% in the 1 Jan 2026 text.
- KOR EUR 20,000 (art. 25a(1)); EU SME scheme EUR 100,000 (art. 25a(2), 25c); joining, crossing the limit and voluntary exit per art. 25a(5), (7), (9).
- Periods (monthly / quarterly / annual: under EUR 1,883 VAT and under EUR 10,000 per intra-EU flow) and deadline: end of the month after the period (AWR art. 10(2), 19(1)); 2026 date table.
- Boxes 1a to 5b; reverse charge (art. 12(2)-(3); Uitvoeringsbesluit art. 24b, 24ba incl. EUR 10,000 electronics); ICP listing (art. 37a, EUR 50,000 quarterly goods limit).
- Suppletie: EUR 1,000 or less in the next return, above that the form within 8 weeks; 5-year window.
- Penalties: EUR 82 late return (max EUR 165, AWR 67b); 3% late payment, min EUR 50, max EUR 6,709 (AWR 67c); vergrijpboete up to 100% (AWR 10a(3)). Belastingrente 5% from 1 Jan 2026 (6.5% in 2025), AWR 30h.
- Examples: (1) bicycle shop Q3 2026 with 21%, 9% and an EU purchase in 4b, pays EUR 2,700; (2) B&B Q1 2026 with the logies change, a EUR 480 correction under the EUR 1,000 threshold and a 3% late-payment penalty of EUR 76.05.

## Sources (all read 2026-10-24)
wetten.overheid.nl: Wet OB 1968 (BWBR0002629), Uitvoeringsbesluit OB 1968 (BWBR0002633), AWR (BWBR0002320), all as in force 1 Jan 2026. belastingdienst.nl: Toelichting btw-aangifte 2026, logies, 9% services, deadlines, aangiftetijdvak, KOR, EU-KOR, ICP period, corrections, penalties, belastingrente, payment, BUA, car.

## Not yet confirmed
- Whether belastingrente is charged on an error of EUR 1,000 or less corrected in a return filed more than 3 months after the year.
- The regulation that sets the 5% interest rate (only the Belastingdienst overview was read).
- The statutory source of the EUR 1,883 / EUR 10,000 annual-return conditions and of the EUR 50 minimum payment penalty (Belastingdienst pages only).
- Conflict noted: the Belastingdienst KOR exit page says a voluntary exit starts on the first day of a return period; art. 25a(7) says the first day of the next calendar quarter at least 4 weeks after notice. The skill follows the law.

## Overlap and contradictions with nl-vat-return (not edited here)
On main, `nl-vat-return.md` has a body identical to the old `netherlands-vat-return.md` v2.0 (only `name`, `last_updated` and a missing `version` key differ). So:

- **Contradiction 1, KOR voluntary exit:** nl-vat-return says it takes effect "only from the first day of a return period"; this skill follows Wet OB art. 25a(7): the first day of the next calendar quarter starting at least 4 weeks after notice.
- **Contradiction 2, culture and sport:** nl-vat-return leaves a possible 2026 change for culture, media and sport open; this skill confirms from the 1 Jan 2026 Tabel I (posts b3, b14) that they stay at 9%.
- **Contradiction 3, penalty figures:** nl-vat-return marks the 2026 penalty amounts as checked on 27 Sept 2026 from Belastingdienst pages only; this skill ties the maxima to AWR art. 67b (EUR 165) and 67c (EUR 6,709).

items.title: fix(cli): keep the Team switch when a configured manifest omits it
items.author: shishenshashen
items.body:
## Motivation

`awr source configure` replaces `.awr/project.toml` with the manifest it is given. `Manifest.team` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "TeamConfig::is_default")]` (`crates/awr-source/src/manifest.rs:24`), so a manifest that omits `[team]` and one that writes `enabled = false` deserialize to the same value. Running `awr source configure` with a manifest that says nothing about Team (one written before the switch existed, or copied from another project) therefore turns Team off without a message.

## Change

- Read the candidate manifest text once as `toml::Value` and test `value.get("team").is_some()` to tell "no `[team]` table" from "explicit `enabled = false`" (`crates/awr-cli/src/source.rs:253-258`).
- When the candidate omits `[team]`, carry the project's current `team` value into the candidate before preview and rendering (`crates/awr-cli/src/source.rs:281-282`); a table that is written explicitly always wins.
- `crates/awr-source/src/manifest.rs` is unchanged: `Manifest.team` keeps its type and serde attributes.

A candidate that writes a `[team]` table without `enabled` counts as explicit: `declares_team_table` sees the table, the carry is skipped, and serde's default (`enabled = false`) applies. That is the same 'an explicit table wins' rule as above, and it is unchanged by this pull request; only a manifest that says nothing about `[team]` at all keeps the project's current switch.

## Tests

New `crates/awr-cli/tests/team_configure.rs`:

- `configure_preserves_team_when_candidate_omits_it`
- `configure_leaves_default_team_alone_when_candidate_omits_it`
- `configure_honours_explicit_team_disabled`

`cargo test -p awr-cli --test team_configure`: 3 passed, 0 failed.

This is 2 files, +139/-4: `crates/awr-cli/src/source.rs` +16/-4 and `crates/awr-cli/tests/team_configure.rs` +123/-0.

CI is the authority for the full workspace: Native platform verification [run 39244258470](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/actions/runs/39244258470) passed on all five platforms (linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos-x64, macos-arm64, windows-x64).

## Note

If you would rather reject `configure` when the candidate omits `[team]` while the project has it enabled, I can change this to a `SourceConflict`.

## Relation to the companion change

This pull request owns the `[team]` switch and the companion change owns `project.context_profile`, both in `crates/awr-cli/src/source.rs`. Each key is decided on its own and neither reads the other, so the two can merge in either order; whichever lands second resolves one shared hunk in the same function.

items.title: feat: protected `attests` on signatures (0.3.1)
items.author: hopeatina
items.body:
## Summary

This adds an optional `attests` field to the protected header of v0.3 Ed25519 signatures. Because it sits inside the signed payload (`protected.attests`), a reader can tell what a signature means and can't be misled about it later.

| `attests` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ingested` | The signer received exactly these bytes: custody and integrity. It is **not** an endorsement of claim level, coverage, verification or acceptance; those remain the producer's claims. |
| `observed` | The signer itself observed or recorded the facts the receipt states, for example its own writes or runs it executed. |
| absent | No statement. The payload is byte-for-byte the same as in 0.3.0. |

Motivation: a host such as OrgX re-signs receipts it imports. Without this field, a valid host signature over an imported receipt that claims `accepted` reads as if the host vouches for the acceptance.

## Changes
- `types.ts`: `AgentWorkSignature.attests`, plus the exported `AGENT_WORK_SIGNATURE_ATTESTATIONS` and `AgentWorkSignatureAttestation`.
- `integrity.ts`: `attests` is included in the canonical signature payload when present and reported per signature in the integrity report. The conformance integrity-report schema is updated to match.
- v0.3 JSON Schema (generated by `scripts/build-v0.3-schema.mjs`): `signature.attests` enum. The v0.1 and v0.2 schemas are unchanged.

items.title: Code follow-ups, a data-fetch script, and the B10 spectrum grade
items.author: ybadr16
items.body:
Three follow-ups.

## 1. Code follow-ups

- **Missing nuclide data is now an error everywhere.**
  - `CrossSectionReader.nuclide_path` raises `FileNotFoundError` for a nuclide with no data file, so a misspelt name (`Pb-208`) can no longer act as vacuum through the Python API. Input files already behaved this way.
  - An MT that the file doesn't contain still reads as 0.
  - Five Pb208 reader tests had passed in CI only because of the old silent zero. They are now marked to skip when there is no data.
- **`main.py`'s source.** It drew θ uniformly on [0, π], which is neither isotropic nor the +x beam that the docs and its TOML twin (`examples/features/mesh_b10_cylinder.toml`) describe. It is now that beam, and its B10 AWR is read from the data instead of 10.0.
- **Hard-coded AWRs.** `validate_secondary.py` passed atomic masses (Be 9.012, Fe 55.845, Pb 207.2) as the AWR in the CM→lab boost.
  - It, `main_benchmark.py` and `analytic_benchmarks.py` now read the AWR from the data.
  - The Pb208 tests use 206.19.
  - The secondary-emission check still agrees with OpenMC (χ²/dof 0.8–1.8), and the analytic benchmarks pass 13/13.
- **Paper draft.** The comment citing results from the untracked paper draft is gone.

## 2. Reproducible data: `tools/fetch_data.py`

- **What it does:**
  - streams OpenMC's official ENDF/B-VIII.0 HDF5 archive (3.4 GB);
  - writes only the requested nuclides: all 50 the repo uses, a set (`--set fixed-source|keff|pincell`), or named ones;
  - checks each file against `tools/endfb-viii.0.sha256`, the snapshot the committed tables were produced with.
- **`--verify`** checks files that are already present.
- **Offline tests** (`tests/test_fetch_data.py`) use a local archive over `file://`.
- **Live test:** fetched three nuclides into an empty directory. It stopped after 2.5 GB, once the last requested file was written, and all three matched the checksums.

## 3. The B10 POOR spectrum was the grader

- **What was wrong:** at 1 keV, OpenMC (analog) leaks nothing below ~0.6 keV. Its spectrum there is 0 ± 0, while PyNeut (implicit capture) resolves that tail at 1e-8 to 4e-5 per source neutron.
  - Those eight empty groups gave 235 of the total χ² of 240.
  - The whole tail is worth only 0.86 expected counts in 10,000 histories.
  - Where OpenMC has counts, χ²/dof was 0.66.
- **The fix:** `compare_spectra` now follows Pearson's rule. It merges groups until each holds at least five expected analog counts, and never takes OpenMC's variance below the Poisson variance.
- **Result:**
  - B10 grades GOOD (0.68), and every case is now GOOD.
  - The integral z-scores are unchanged.
  - The only other grade change is Al27 at 14 MeV, from 2.1 (FAIR) to 2.0 (GOOD).
  - A ±20 % shape tilt still grades POOR (`tests/test_spectrum_grading.py`).
- **Also fixed:** `validate_mixture.py` had been broken since the tally PR removed `_pyneut_spectrum`. It now shares `run_scored` with the main suite and agrees with OpenMC (z 0.1 / 0.2, spectrum GOOD).

## Tests

- **With the ENDF data:** 264 passed, 6 skipped (the skipped tests need OpenMC).
- **Without the data, as CI runs:** 223 passed, 47 skipped.
- **CI:** green on 3.10 and 3.12.

Alle Weiterentwicklungen seit icoglu/BORA-Rodaten-Optimizer#2.

### Paketregeln
- **Regel 1 – AWR-Aufzeichnungszeitraum:** Je AWR-Report (HTML/Text) ein Paket `BORA_JJJJ-MM-TT_HHMM-HHMM.zip` für Begin–End Snap; automatisch nach jedem Upload/Einlesen, nur betroffene Zeiträume werden neu erstellt, ungültige entfernt.

- **Alle weiteren Dateien, die zum Zeitrahmen passen**, kommen vollständig unter `sonstige/` ins Paket.
- Tages-Pakete optional (`BORA_DAY_PACKAGES=1`); Altbestand ohne AWR wird entfernt.

### Inhaltsprüfung
- Alle Dateien werden im **Inhalt** auf das Datum geprüft: Logs zeilenweise (Zeilenanfang, sonst ganze Zeile, z. B. JSON-Logs), Text/CSV/JSON/XML/HTML vollständig, Office-Dokumente, PDF, sonstige Binärdateien (lesbare Textstellen); `.gz`/`.bz2`/`.xz` transparent.

- Keine Redundanzen: identische Dateien und derselbe Report als HTML+TXT nur einmal.
- Einheitlicher Zeitstempel für ZIP und alle Einträge.
- EAR/WAR/JAR/RAR werden nicht entpackt und ignoriert.
- Upload-Fortschritt als Balkendiagramm (gesamt + je Datei) und Prozentanzeige der Verarbeitung; Browser überträgt das Original-Änderungsdatum.

items.author: zenaror
items.body:
RUN 43 executed `sync-0001` (`GBP-AUDIO-012`) from slot `22-sync` on the physical
GameCube + Game Boy Player with the Yoshi's Island cartridge. This Issue fixes
what will be read, how, and in what order.

**The Operator's declaration is already posted verbatim** (#119
`issuecomment-...`, "the Operator's declaration"), before any figure was opened.
That order is satisfied, so the verdicts may be computed.

---

## 1. Artefacts

Delivered from the card. The Operator was mid-way through another automated test
and asked the Orchestrator to copy them; copied with `cp --update=none`, the
originals on the card untouched, both sides hashed.

```text
logs/run43/GBP-AUDIO-012_sync-0001.log       151 285 B  fd0652c36d6b0d649fc58b0db4aab844287d2121067ca3e22d63208a252ae4bc
logs/run43/GBP-AUDIO-012_sync-0001-awr.bin 2 621 580 B  a70ce4c11effad1c843a9dca49b76f9cf2f2eafc7c5becf4567071a7af735f80
run43-gecko.txt (Orchestrator's live capture)  3 221 B  (hash in the pre-ingestion report)
```

`2 621 580 = 640 x 4096 + 140`. Image: `sync-0001`, commit `8bb0d46`, slot
`22-sync`, `boot.dol` 543 264 B `ab902f6f…0941`, verified from the medium by all
three of Executor, Orchestrator and Operator.

**Archive flat and run-suffixed**, as #115 §4 decided, with the `GBP-HW-272`
recount in the same round:

```text
captures/local/GBP-AUDIO-012_sync-0001-run43.log
captures/local/GBP-AUDIO-012_sync-0001-run43-awr.bin
captures/local/GECKO-LIVE-run43-orchestrator-capture.txt
```

---

## 2. What the run produced, and what it did not

```text
Phase 1     COMPLETE   18 switches, 18 answers
ride-along  COMPLETE   640 raw blocks of a real game's audio
Phase 2     1 confirmed setting of 3      -> INCONCLUSIVE by (t4), as frozen
Phase 3     depths=0, never ran
stop        event_store_cap               z=0: the Operator did nothing wrong
```

**The early stop is an Orchestrator design defect and is recorded as one.** The
session was budgeted in time (300 + 240 + 138 against 720 s) and never in events;
the event store's 16 384 entries were a second, harder cap that no phase budget
could satisfy. **All three phases could never have completed at any pace.**

It is the third instance in this pre-registration of freezing a mechanism without
working its arithmetic, and the first to reach hardware. §V27.13's own rule
covers it exactly, and was written one amendment earlier.

---

## 3. What is computed, and what each thing means

### Phase 1 — the falsifier, and the run's reason for existing

Frozen in §V27.10, unchanged:

```text
D = real switches judged in the PREDICTED direction, of 12
    (SAME counts as NOT in the predicted direction)

D >= 10     CONFIRMS      P = 79/4096 = 0.0193 under the conservative binary null
D <= 6      REFUTES
D = 7,8,9   UNRESOLVED

guard   nulls judged a change >= 4 of 6 -> INCONCLUSIVE regardless of D
```

**Report `D`, the null count, and the per-switch table.** `A = "Sim percebi"`
says a difference was perceptible; it says **nothing** about direction and must
not be read as support for either verdict.

### Phase 2 — one setting, and it still measures something

The confirmed `TARGET`, in samples, is the measurement. With one setting there is
no spread and no verdict, but **a single number with a stated uncertainty is not
nothing** — it is the only end-to-end measurement of this offset that exists.

**Resolve his `B` against the log and say which reading holds:**

```text
confirmed AT the floor (384)     -> he called ~250-283 ms of remaining chain
                                    "synchronised"; the unaccounted residue is
                                    bounded ABOVE by that, measured rather than
                                    modelled
confirmed ABOVE the floor        -> the confirmed TARGET is the measurement, and
                                    his memory of the floor belongs to the
                                    exploration
```

Report the exploration path too — every step, not only the confirm — since with
one setting the path is most of the information.

### Phase 3 — nothing

`depths=0`. Report it as absent. **Do not infer anything about the correction's
floor from Phase 2's exploration**: Phase 2's floor is 384 by construction and
was never intended to reach the correction's limit.

### `M1`–`M4`

As frozen. `M1` failing voids the perceptual results. Report the per-arm loss
rates outside any instrument window, per `GBP-HW-338`/`GBP-HW-339`.

### The ride-along — `U-GBP-012`'s game half

640 raw blocks decoded **at all sixteen slices**, not only by pairs, because a
game may set `SOUNDBIAS` above 32.768 kHz. Compare against the block decode as
`GBP-HW-340` did for the tones: energy above 2 048 Hz, the harmonic structure,
and whether the folding `GBP-HW-340` found on tones appears on real game audio.

**This is the first measurement of a real game's audio bandwidth that will
exist.** Its Hz axis inherits `U-GBP-041`, and 0.16 s is short — say what that
does to the frequency resolution rather than leaving a reader to assume.

---

## 4. What this run does NOT settle

- **`U-GBP-046` is not closed by a CONFIRMS.** Phase 1 establishes that the
  cushion moves the perceived offset; the residue needs Phase 2's measurement
  with more than one setting.
- **The correction's floor is unmeasured.** Phase 3 is the only thing that would
  have measured it and it did not run. `U-GBP-045`'s cost side stays open.
- `TARGET` is not changed in the runtime. This run measures.
- Phase 6 is not reopened.

---

## 5. The re-run question is NOT decided here

Whether Phases 2 and 3 need a second image depends on what Phase 1 says, and the
next pre-registration has to be built on the **event rate this log actually
shows** — events per second, what produces them, and what session length 16 384
permits. **Derive that number in this ingestion.** It is a capacity fact, not a
gate figure, and it is the thing that was missing the first time.

---

## 6. Delegation

Commits and pushes delegated. Small commit

- `parse_mlsx_time` accepts the optional fraction of RFC 3659 §2.3 (`time-val = 14DIGIT [ "." 1*DIGIT ]`) and keeps it as sub-second precision (digits beyond nanoseconds are ignored). FileZilla Server sends milliseconds, so every MLSD line from it failed with `InvalidDate` and listings came back empty.
- `parse_mlsx` takes the pathname as everything after the first `"; "` (RFC 3659 §7.2: `[ facts ] SP pathname`; a fact value can't contain `;`). Before, a name with `;` lost everything up to its last `;`. Lines without facts (starting with the SP) are handled too; lines without `"; "` keep the previous behaviour.

Tests: fractional seconds (milliseconds, more than nine digits), invalid fractions, names with `;` and several spaces, a name with a leading space, an MLST line without facts.

Checked with real lines from FileZilla Server 1.12.6, e.g. `type=file;size=27;modify=20261014180643.693;perms=awr; liesmich.txt` – rejected by 12.2.0, parsed by this branch.

items.title: fix(state): tally deliverables from the whole output tree
items.author: apskis
items.body:
## Why

The 2026-09-12 run printed `[state] deliverables on disk: awareness=2` while five awareness posts existed in the output. `update_state.py` carried the same narrow assumption PR #2 removed from `pending_deliverables.py`: it looked only in each kind's canonical folder, so a post the builder saved under `awareness/`, `awareness/2026/` or `bulletins/2026/` was invisible to the tally, the deliverables index and the next ID computation.

## What changed

- `collect()` walks the whole output tree and skips only `state/`, so a scratch draft never counts as output and a deliverable saved off path still does.
- Files are ordered newest first, so where an ID exists in more than one place the index names the copy the pipeline wrote last.
- The summary line counts distinct IDs rather than files: one post saved to two folders is one post.
- Any ID found in more than one place is printed with every copy, so a path drift shows up in the run log instead of quietly skewing the index.
- `new this run` no longer lists an ID twice when it was saved twice.

## Verification

Fixture with a real `.docx` in `employee-posts/`, a second copy of the same ID in `awareness/2026/`, a scratch copy in `state/_work/`, and a hunt package:

```
[state] deliverables on disk: awareness=1, hunt=1
[state] AWR-2026-09-12 (awareness) has 2 copies, newest first:
        ['awareness/2026/AWR-...-Stray.docx', 'employee-posts/AWR-...-Real.docx']
[state] new this run: ['AWR-2026-09-12', 'TH26-03']
```

Distinct count correct, scratch excluded, stray counted and reported, no duplicate entry in the new list.

## Companion cleanup, applied to S3 directly

Sixteen awareness `.docx` files were scattered across the bucket root, `awareness/`, `awareness/2026/`, `awareness/blog/2026/` and `bulletins/2026/`. All sixteen were moved under `employee-posts/_variants/<origin folder>/`, preserving the originating folder in the path. Nothing was deleted and the bucket is versioned. No awareness file now sits outside `employee-posts/` or `state/`.

Which variant is the real post for 2026-09-10, 09-11 and 09-12 is an editorial call and was deliberately left to the author rather than guessed: there are up to seven differing copies per date.

`state/dedup-log.md` and `state/awareness-topic-ledger.md` carry no file paths, so neither needed correcting. `state/deliverables-index.md` has one pre-existing stale row for AWR-2026-09-10 naming a path that has not existed since the drift began; it was left alone because the row's intended target cannot be identified among the candidates.

items.title: init-scaffolded .awr/intake/ sources are documented as source files, but work create/progress/complete reject them as runtime-owned
items.author: FreeOnePlus
items.body:
## Summary

On a blank project, `awr init --accept` scaffolds the goal and the work ledger under `.awr/intake/`. [TAKEOVER.md](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/docs/dev/TAKEOVER.md#L24) calls these "source files, not disposable runtime state", and content review explicitly supports "authored `.awr/intake/` sources". But every AWR write path that changes a work item (`work create`, `work progress`, `work complete`) rejects any ledger under `.awr/` as runtime-owned. A freshly initialized project therefore cannot use AWR's own work lifecycle until the ledger is moved out of `.awr/`, and nothing in the output says so.

## Environment

- AWR 0.4.0 built from `main` at 230c51b1 (`cargo build --locked -p awr-cli`), macOS arm64.
- Also seen with the source-built 0.4.0 / schema 14 runtime at e8fa30ec98a5, so this is not new.
- Throwaway project, no pre-existing sources.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir demo
awr --project "$PWD/demo" init --accept
ls -A demo/.awr/intake        # GOALS.md  inventory.json  project.toml  work-ledger.yaml

# 1. create new work
awr --project "$PWD/demo" work create --title "Demo task" --request-key demo-1
# RuleViolation: rule violation: runtime files cannot be task sources
```

2. Add a task to `demo/.awr/intake/work-ledger.yaml` by hand (that is what `INTAKE-001`'s `next_action` asks for), run `awr source reindex`, start a session with `--claim` on it, then record progress:

```sh
awr --project "$PWD/demo" work progress DEMO-001 --session <SESSION> --expected-revision <REV> \
  --reason r --next-action n --response-view summary
```

Result:

```json
{ "code": "proposal_required",
  "error": { "details": { "proposal_id": "...",
                          "reason": "runtime-owned files cannot be source mutation targets",
                          "source_write_performed": false } } }
```

3. Apply the status change by hand (`status: in_progress`), reindex, register evidence and run `work complete`. It returns the same `proposal_required`. (Before the hand edit it fails with `InvalidTransition: cannot Complete work with source state Ready`, a consequence of step 2 not being able to record progress.)

4. The proposal left behind by step 2 stays `approved` in `awr proposal list`, and `awr proposal apply <id> ...` returns `proposal_required` again, so it can never be applied.

## Expected

The scaffold behaves as the docs describe (mapped YAML writes obey the usual claim / revision / completion checks), or it is created somewhere AWR is allowed to write. At the very least the failure tells the user what to do.

## Why it happens

The same directory is treated differently by different subsystems:

- Mutations reject everything under `.awr/`: [yaml_create.rs L74-L76](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/crates/awr-source/src/yaml_create.rs#L74-L76), [yaml_mutation.rs L147-L149](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/crates/awr-source/src/yaml_mutation.rs#L147-L149), [mutation_apply.rs L555](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/crates/awr-runtime/src/mutation_apply.rs#L555).
- Content review exempts `.awr/intake` ([content_review.rs L29-L31](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/crates/awr-source/src/content_review.rs#L29-L31)), and so do the docs ([TAKEOVER.md L24](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/docs/dev/TAKEOVER.md#L24), [content-review.md L37](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/docs/dev/reference/content-review.md#L37)).
- `init` can only create files under that prefix, and the reviewed-draft flow cannot redirect them: after `init --write-draft`, rewriting `generated_files` and `authority_mapping.sources[].path` to project-owned paths and running `init --from-draft ... --accept` fails with `RuleViolation: draft may create only the four owned intake source files` ([onboarding.rs L597-L604](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/crates/awr-cli/src/onboarding.rs#L597-L604)).

## Workaround

`awr source relocate --source <ledger-source-id> --to work-ledger.yaml` works for the YAML ledger (the destination is a byte-identical copy, given as a relative path). It keeps the work item identities and the active claim, and afterwards `work progress`, `evidence add` and `work complete` all write through. It is documented in [host-contract.md](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/docs/dev/reference/host-contract.md#L159), but neither the intake docs nor the error mention it. The Markdown goal source cannot be relocated (`Unsupported: adapter keys depend on the old locator`, [source_relocation.rs L139](https://github.com/originoneai/awr/blob/230c51b17951705b60dcd65b4a9fb018582364fa/crates/awr-cli/src/source_relocation.rs#L139)), which matches the documented "path-derived keys are unsupported".

## Suggested directions

1. Treat authored `.awr/intake/` sources as mutable, consistent with content review and the docs: narrow the `.awr` prefix guard to actual runtime state (`state.db*`, `mutations/`, `artifacts/`, `cache/`, ...).
2. Or scaffold into a project-owned location, for example a root-level `work-ledger.yaml` with the placeholder goal embedded (the "small project" shape already shown in TAKEOVER.md), and let a reviewed draft choose the paths.
3. In any case, make the failure actionable: name `source relocate` with the exact command in the `RuleViolation` / `proposal_required` message, and avoid leaving an `approved` proposal behind that cannot be applied.
